producer_report.summary: Added a reading size gate. Root cause: reading validation never compared a reading's scope with the producer and verifier deadlines, so multi-item sources yielded readings no single run could finish. Fix: a private helper `check_reading_size` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, called from `build_reading` right after `reader.validate()`. It runs only when the reading names a capability, so a decline is not gated. It refuses when the reading's own `wall_time_s.p50` is strictly greater than the smaller of `budget.producer_timeout_s` and `budget.verifier_timeout_s`. The error names the exceeded timeout and says to pick one deliverable and name the rest as follow-up requests in out_of_scope. The existing one-time correction in `read_with_correction` feeds this back to the reader, so no loop change was needed. I added four tests that call the real `build_reading` with the shipped athena.toml and defaults.toml: a producer-only refusal, a verifier-only refusal, acceptance within both deadlines (p50 30 and exactly 2400), and a decline with an oversize forecast that is accepted. CHANGELOG.md has a new entry under [Unreleased] / Added. outputs.rs and config.rs are unchanged. No config keys were added.

checks_run.note: First run: the two refusal tests failed because the message had a capital 'Pick one deliverable' and the tests looked for lowercase. I changed the message to 'finish it: pick one deliverable ...'.
20 passed, including the 4 new tests. The earlier run had the other 90 reading tests passing.
The call showed no non-zero exit code. The output was too long to display and was saved to a file I am not allowed to read, so I did not check each 'test result' line myself. Athena reruns it.

criteria_check.criterion: The change description and a doc comment on the gate in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs name the root cause: reading validation never compared reading scope with the producer/verifier deadline; the fix sits in build_reading.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment on `check_reading_size` in reading.rs says: 'Root cause: reading validation never compared the reading's scope with the producer and verifier deadlines ... the fix sits in `build_reading`'. The CHANGELOG.md entry and my summary say the same. Checked by reading both.

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in athena-core builds a reading whose forecast wall_time_s.p50 exceeds budget.producer_timeout_s and asserts build_reading returns an error whose message tells the reader to pick one deliverable and name the rest as follow-up requests. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib reading::tests::a_re`: `a_reading_forecasting_more_than_the_producer_timeout_is_refused_with_advice_to_pick_one_deliverable` passes. It uses p50 5000 against a producer timeout of 3000 and asserts the error contains 'pick one deliverable', 'follow-up request' and 'producer_timeout_s of 3000s'. It fails without the gate because `unwrap_err` would panic on Ok.

criteria_check.criterion: A companion test shows a reading with p50 within both deadlines is still accepted, and a test with p50 above only verifier_timeout_s is refused; the oversize tests fail if the gate is removed and use a generic oversize forecast, not one job's data. Run cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core --lib reading::tests::a_re`. `a_reading_within_both_timeouts_is_accepted` passes for p50 30 and 2400, and also asserts the recorded p50 equals the input. `a_reading_forecasting_more_than_only_the_verifier_timeout_is_refused` passes with p50 2700 against producer 3000 and verifier 2400. `a_decline_is_not_held_to_the_deadlines` passes. The forecasts are generic numbers from a made-up README reading.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more readings and the higher refusal rate is intended: expected 3% of newly refused readings (only readings forecasting a p50 wall time beyond a configured timeout).  Existing tests and the default athena.toml readings still pass: cargo test --workspace.
criteria_check.evidence: The gate refuses only a p50 strictly above the smaller timeout, and only for readings that name a capability. The CHANGELOG entry states the intended rise in refusals, about 3% (estimate, not measured). `cargo test --workspace --locked` ran once and showed no non-zero exit; I could not read its saved output to confirm each result line. Athena reruns it.

criteria_check.criterion: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets and cargo test --workspace all pass.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` with no output or errors. `cargo test --workspace --locked` showed no non-zero exit code.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md records the new reading size gate.
criteria_check.evidence: CHANGELOG.md has a new first bullet under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added`, 'A reading size gate.' It gives the root cause, the fix (`check_reading_size` in `build_reading`), the rule, the retry message, and the intended rise in refusals.

open_issues: The 3% newly-refused figure is an estimate from the request. Nothing measures it, and the CHANGELOG labels it as such.
mistakes: The first message started the advice with a capital 'Pick one deliverable' while my tests looked for lowercase. I changed the message to 'finish it: pick one deliverable ...'. This was caught by the first test run.
I could not read the saved full workspace test output, so I did not verify each result line of `cargo test --workspace --locked`. I only saw that the call showed no non-zero exit code.
learnings: `build_reading` never uses `self`, so tests can call it on an `Athena` from `test_support::make_athena` with a never-called script closure `Box::new(|_| unreachable!(..))`; this compiles.

`JobConfig` has all-pub fields, so a test can build it from `Config::parse(include_str!("../../../athena.toml"))` and `DefaultsModel::parse(include_str!("../../../defaults.toml"))` and then edit `config.budget` timeouts.
The shipped timeouts are producer 3000s and verifier 2400s, so the effective limit is 2400s on p50.
The hook that restricts reads to the working directory also blocks reading Bash's saved large-output files.
desires: A way to read the full output of a long cargo test run, for example a quiet flag that prints only the result lines.
